newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy minister--no decision yet on cordless phones.
newsitem.headline: Italy minister--no decision yet on cordless phones.

text.p: Italian Post ministry undersecretary Michele Lauria said the government has not yet defined the authorisation rules for cordless phones, following the interest shown early on Wednesday by Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM).

He also added that as well as TIM and Telecom Italia, the Infostrada joint venture between Olivetti and U.S. Bell Atlantic had shown interest in advanced cordless phone systems using the Digital European Cordless Telephony (DECT) standard.
Lauria added that the European Community directive 96/2 includes DECT among the mobile services it deregulated as of July 1, 1996 and any authorisation must conform to this ruling.
Earlier on Wednesday, TIM's managing director Vito Gamberale asked the Italian Post Ministry for authorisation to offer a cordless phone service.

In October TIM's sister company Telecom Italia announced plans to launch a cordless phone, but this move immediately sparked controversy when anti-trust chairman Giuliano Amato said that if it went ahead it would be taking advantage of Telecom Italia's dominant position in the fixed line market and compete head-on with mobile phone companies.
Both TIM and Telecom Italia are majority-owned by state-controlled telecoms holding company STET.
